claim: Developers formulate hypotheses poorly without aids: only 11% correct at stage 1, 25% at stage 2, 39% at stage 3 (20 control sessions, median 1-2 hypotheses).
agent_test: Log a hypothesis before any run; score fraction correct against token budget.

claim: A correct hypothesis at stage two raises the odds of fixing the defect about 5x (p=0.01, 60 sessions). This is correlational, not causal.
agent_test: Compare success when the agent must write a testable hypothesis vs free search, at equal tokens.

claim: Giving developers candidate hypotheses helped (OR 6.24, p=0.03). Giving only fault locations did not (OR 1.4, p=0.64; fix rate p=0.67).
agent_test: Arm A: scaffold generates several candidate causes. Arm B: only location hints.

claim: Observed professional debugging is mostly manual run-and-observe (84% manual runs, state inspected about twice per episode). Self-report says developers follow hypothesis then test. Source conflict on how formal real practice is.
agent_test: Compare agent logs with and without a forced prediction line.

claim: A hypothesis, prediction, experiment, observation, conclusion loop with real execution (AutoSD) gives no clear accuracy win over a plain strong LLM: 113 vs 110 on Defects4J v2.0, but 76 vs 87 on v1.2. It helps on a self-built benchmark (189 vs 179 plausible) and with stronger models. A second use (Straubinger 2025, mutant-killing tests, gpt-4o-mini) found the hypothesis loop matched plain iterative retry in success (~60%) and cost more tokens.
agent_test: Equal-token A/B of plain repair vs the predict-observe loop on a held-out bug set.

claim: Real execution output is what makes the loop work. With model-simulated debugger output, plausible-patch runs fall from 73% to 63%, and a DONE conclusion flips from +12.4 points to -11 points as a signal. LDB (GPT-3.5, StarCoder) also finds model-simulated traces add 0 or -0.6 points where real traces add +0.6 to +9.1.
agent_test: Ablate real tool output vs model-simulated output at equal tokens.

claim: A model-stated DONE conclusion after real experiments tracks correctness a little: 89% correct with DONE vs 82% without, among plausible patches. Older code-model confidence is poorly calibrated (ECE 0.09 to 0.73, Spiess 2024); no test on 2025 reasoning models.
agent_test: Check whether a conclusion token predicts correctness on our agent.

claim: Many refutations in the scientific loop come from broken experiments: of 25 cases where all hypotheses were rejected, 13 had breakpoints never hit by the test. A second count (DoVer, multi-agent hypotheses): 57.6 to 66.7% of intervention trials on hard sets were Inconclusive, mostly because the intervention was not carried out.
schema_part: G (validate the experiment before trusting a refutation)
agent_test: Add an experiment-validity check (did the probe run?) and count wrong rejections.

claim: Hypothesis-style explanations raised patch-review accuracy for developers in 5 of 6 real bugs (N=20), with no time difference. Some wrong patches were accepted without scrutiny.
agent_test: Human-facing output only; not an agent test.

claim: LLM self-repair on its own feedback is a weak gain: GPT-4 repair success 33.3% with own feedback vs 52.6% with human feedback. Self-repair is about equal to equal-budget sampling (0.97x to 1.05x).
agent_test: Compare self-critique with an independent fresh sample at equal tokens.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without an external signal does not help and can hurt (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0). With oracle labels it helps, which is an unrealistic signal. Tool-based checking (CRITIC) is the working route.
schema_part: G (no self-verdict without an external check)
agent_test: Run revise-without-evidence vs revise-with-test at equal tokens.
audit_note: Oracle numbers are listed inconsistently in the evidence (b21/c14 give GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 95.5; the paper table shows 84.3), but the claim quotes only the intrinsic numbers, which match.

claim: Concrete debugger access helps strong LLMs: Claude 3.7 Sonnet on SWE-bench-Lite 37.2 to 48.4 (52.1 if pdb is unlocked after 5 rewrites). It hurts weaker models (GPT-4o 19.1 to 17.2; GPT-4o-mini 4.0 to 3.5). Llama-3.3-70B went 2.4 to 4.0 against the paper's own prose. Debug2Fix (2026): with GPT-5, Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, a debug subagent raised GitBug-Java pass rate (GPT-5 60.2 to 73.1); raw debug tools did not (Sonnet -14.8% relative); optional-use rates were as low as 8%.
agent_test: Give the agent a probe tool after a failed attempt; compare with rewrite-only at equal tokens.

claim: Interactive debugger dialogue works: ChatDBG fix rate 57% (bare why?), 67% (targeted question), 85% with one follow-up. For C/C++, 36% of suggestions fix the root cause and 55% more fix the proximate cause.
agent_test: Allow one follow-up probe round and compare.

claim: Trace or runtime-state feedback helps LLM repair by modest, model-dependent amounts: LDB +9.1 over seed on HumanEval with GPT-3.5, +2.4 with GPT-4; plain Self-Debug about 0 on StarCoder; NExT +26.1 on Mbpp-R. Zero-shot trace CoT can hurt (-7.8 on average).
agent_test: Compare trace-informed vs no-trace repair at equal tokens on a weak and a strong model.
audit_note: In Zhong et al. Table 2 the +2.4 is for GPT-4-generated seed programs debugged with a GPT-3.5 backbone, not LDB run with GPT-4.

claim: Explaining code line by line gives small repair gains: Spider +2-3 points, TransCoder +2-3; unit-test feedback up to +12.
agent_test: Ablate the explanation step at equal tokens.

claim: Most LLMs are weak at predicting program behaviour, the core of predict-then-observe. CRUXEval GPT-4 with CoT about 75% input and 81% output prediction; best open models under 50%; REval average accuracy 44.4%. Higher complexity lowers scores.
agent_test: Measure the agent's pre-run prediction accuracy; trust predictions only above a threshold.
audit_note: Abstract gives Code Llama 34B at 50% input prediction, so 'best open models under 50%' is a rounding borderline (table values ~47/44 without CoT).

claim: Logic and multi-bug errors are much harder for LLMs than syntax errors, and runtime feedback helps syntax and reference bugs but not logic bugs.
agent_test: Break results by bug type; test whether probes help logic errors.

claim: Agent-computer interface design matters: SWE-agent gets 18.0% vs 11.0% shell-only on SWE-bench-Lite; linted edits and summarised search help.
agent_test: Equal-token test of tool format variants.
audit_note: The 18.0% vs 11.0% and linting/summarised-search ablation numbers are correct, but both matching sources are the same SWE-agent paper; AutoCodeRover and RepairAgent do not test interface design.

claim: Reflection after failed tests helps only when tests are reliable: Reflexion HumanEval 0.80 to 0.91, MBPP Python 0.80 to 0.77; MBPP false-positive rate 0.16 vs 0.01.
agent_test: Vary test-suite quality and measure the gain from reflection.

claim: People test mostly confirming cases (Wason); positive testing is often sound (Klayman and Ha). LLMs are also weak at experiment design and exploration (BoxingGym, bandit study) and show human-like Wason content effects.
agent_test: Force one test designed to break the leading hypothesis; compare against free testing.

claim: Closed reason-act-observe loops cut hallucination (ReAct 0% vs 56% in CoT failures on HotpotQA). Hypothesis-refine with a symbolic interpreter raises inductive accuracy (ACRE 28 to 59).
agent_test: Compare a closed observe loop with pure CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Whyline-style why-did and why-didn't questions sped up human debugging in one small test (Ko and Myers 2004, PDF read): 4 users with vs 4 without; debug time cut by a mean factor of 7.8 over six matched scenarios (F(1,5)=12.64, p<.02); tasks done 3.20 vs 2.25 (t(7)=3.0, p<.02). 50% of errors in formative studies came from false hypotheses.
agent_test: Have the agent ask why-not against the expected output; test.

claim: No controlled test in this evidence shows that following the Zeller scientific-debugging protocol speeds humans up. The method is prescriptive.
agent_test: Run protocol vs free-form as an A/B on the agent.

claim: Gap 1 stays open. No study isolates the written prediction step. The nearest ablation (hypothesis loop vs plain retry: equal success, higher cost) suggests a bundled predict loop is not free accuracy.
agent_test: Equal-token A/B: same agent with and without a required pre-run prediction.

claim: Wrong pre-run self-prediction can harm repair. When the model simulates execution itself, gains are zero or negative on weaker models (StarCoder -0.6 / 0.0) while real traces help (+0.6 to +9.1). Even strong models predict intermediate program state much worse than final output (REval mean 44.4%, IC 10.3; GPT-4-Turbo 75.0%, IC 42.5).
agent_test: Log predicted vs observed output on the agent's own runs; measure whether prediction error precedes a wrong fix.
audit_note: Minor: StarCoder SD null/negative result is HumanEval only (SD helped on MBPP), and LDB's +0.6 to +9.1 is the HumanEval range (paper says up to +9.8 overall); 44.4/10.3 are model averages while 75.0/42.5 is GPT-4-Turbo.

claim: Probe access is gated by adoption as much as by model strength. Claude Sonnet 4.5 called an optional debug subagent in 8% of SWE-Bench-Live instances. Blocking edits until one debug call raised call rate to about 99% and GPT-5 pass rate from 60.2 to 73.1 on GitBug-Java.
agent_test: Add a hard gate: no patch before one executed probe; compare with optional probes.

claim: LLM predictions of outcomes are only mildly better than chance and still useful as a filter: pairwise ML-solution preference 61.5% (chance 50%), yet predict-then-verify converged about 6x faster than execution-only (ForeAgent). Prediction must be verified.
agent_test: Use predictions to rank probes, then run the top one; never replace the run.

claim: Hypotheses made from reading logs with no run are unreliable: step-attribution accuracy 24% (GPT-4o) and 7% (GPT-5) on 14 cases with ambiguous truth, 44% and 53% on 15 clear cases (DoVer, 29 cases).
agent_test: Require an executed check for every blame claim.

claim: Runtime feedback does not help logic bugs because raw errors are too low-level (DebugBench). No study tests whether a stated expectation fixes this. Gap 10 only partly closed.
agent_test: For logic bugs force an explicit expected-behaviour statement before reading output; compare with plain feedback.

claim: Gaps 5, 6, 8 and 9 remain open after this pass: no LLM debugging study varies confirm vs disconfirm tests; no causal test of the 5x hypothesis result and no trial of LLM-supplied candidate hypotheses; Gould, Vessey, Gugerty and Olson, Katz and Anderson, Parnin and Orso not obtained; no replication of AutoSD found. The search quota ran out.
agent_test: Run these directly on our agent instead of waiting for literature.
